synopsis: The strategy must establish a virtual performance baseline for the existing detector, but raw sensor-log replay measures only recorded sensors, mounting positions and scenarios; changes to sensor modality, mounting or processing prevent fair direct comparison of raw detections and per-sensor statistics [f25, f95, f107]. Detection is necessary for braking but insufficient for complete safety: vehicle-and-person detection leaves environmental interactions unaddressed, and passing detection or ISO 3450 brake tests does not establish overall human-machine or perception-system performance [f11302, f11575, f3487, f2361]. ISO 16001:2017 requires unambiguous, uninterrupted detection signals and detection within 300 ms, while detection, confirmation, risk computation and intervention initiation consume distance before deceleration builds; nevertheless, reviewed standards supply no detection or false-alarm sample sizes, and South Africa's Regulation 8.10 supplies no numerical detection or false-alarm thresholds [f2403, f2405, f6052, f5160, f2281]. Environmental robustness remains uncertain: 2023–2026 construction and mining studies report lidar degradation in real dust, and on-road evidence includes complete pedestrian-detection loss with high-visibility clothing in tests reported on 16 October 2025; these findings should not be treated as quantified off-road performance [f6688, f7980]. Credible validation therefore needs explicit object-class and exclusion records, real-versus-simulated dust correlation, and real-data results by condition bin with confidence intervals; ideal sensor models and object-list replay can conceal raw-sensor deficiencies or assume perception has already succeeded [f8008, f10562, f10566, f4480, f5259].
